correctness.rationale: For N divisible by three, any N/3-line cover must partition E(F_q) into distinct collinear zero-sum triples; the total group sum excludes exactly groups with a unique involution. Cichacz Theorem 12 supplies zero-sum 3-partitions for all other groups. In the excluded case, a quotient onto Z/3 and a Goddyn--Halasz near transversal on its kernel produce N/3-1 disjoint zero-sum triples; two rational lines cover the three remaining points. This attains N/3+1. The explicit cyclic construction is verified for k=1..500; complete line-set-cover calculations check six small elliptic cubics. Finite checks do not prove the general result; the group existence theorems were independently verified in their source statements.

originality.rationale: The 2026 paper poses the finite-field rational-line-cover problem and explicitly states only N/3+O(1) for odd-order plane elliptic cubic groups. The already-known zero-sum 3-partition theorem supplies the exact-cover existence condition but not the exceptional sharp one-additional-line construction. The already-known near-transversal theorem supplies the complementary ingredient but does not mention curve line covers. Their assembly yields a complete exact geometric covering dichotomy across all point counts divisible by three. No equivalent explicit statement was identified in the inspected literature, accessible own findings or focused published record search; historical priority cannot be guaranteed.
residual_risks: Historical priority may overlap an unlocated prior short corollary combining 3-ZSP and near transversals with plane cubic chord laws.
The 2019 group-table theorem is the key external nontrivial existence ingredient; the proof assumes its published validity.
A prior source on finite elliptic line coverings outside the examined materials could contain the same exact formula.

value.rationale: A natural covering invariant for all smooth plane elliptic cubics with rational flex and 3-divisible point count is classified exactly, not estimated asymptotically. The full obstruction and sharp one-line exceptional gap are independent of field order and provide a structural test via 2-torsion in the finite elliptic group. The result gives both infinite families and an explicit construction in the cyclic exceptional subfamily; this answers the motivating exact-cover question in a mathematically coherent arithmetic regime, with applications to line-cover algorithms.
